commit.message: Find the Claude CLI where people actually install it (0.4.1)

findings.title: nvm fallback in doctor.sh will miss the symlinked claude binary
findings.description: npm-installed global bins under `.nvm/versions/node/<v>/bin/` are symlinks into `lib/node_modules/...`, so `-type f` filters out exactly the case this branch exists to catch. `tail -1` also picks the last path in `find` order rather than the newest Node version, so even when it does match it can report an outdated CLI. The result is a doctor that says "no claude binary found anywhere" for the nvm users it was written for.
findings.suggestion: Consider accepting symlinks and sorting by version, e.g. `\( -type f -o -type l \)` piped through `sort -V`.

findings.title: Version-manager directories are sorted lexicographically, not by version
findings.description: The comment promises "newest first", but `entries.sort().reverse()` is a string sort: with `v9.11.2`, `v18.20.0`, `v20.11.0` under `.nvm/versions/node`, `v9.11.2` sorts last and therefore comes first after `.reverse()`. A stale `claude` shim left behind by an old Node version would be preferred over the current one — and since `locateClaude` returns the first candidate that answers `--version`, that stale CLI wins outright.
findings.suggestion: Consider a numeric-aware comparison so `v18` and `v20` sort above `v9`, e.g. `localeCompare(..., { numeric: true })` in descending order. Copying before sorting also avoids mutating the array returned by `readdirSync`.

findings.title: Every candidate is spawned twice on the failure path
findings.description: `anyRunnable` probes candidates with `--version` (15s timeout each) purely to decide whether to consult the login shell, and then the loop at line 187 re-probes the very same paths. In the common bad case — several stale paths exist but none work — each is executed twice, and the candidate list just grew to include one entry per installed Node version. Combined with the 10s login-shell probe this can stall activation for a long time.
findings.suggestion: Consider having the probe return the working path (or the index it stopped at) and reusing it, so a candidate is never executed twice: e.g. hoist the `--version` probe into a helper that returns `{ path, stdout } | null` and feed its result to both the shell-fallback decision and the version parsing. Shorter per-candidate timeouts for the speculative pass would also help.

findings.title: An invalid CODE_BIN prints two contradictory errors
findings.description: `find_code` runs inside a command substitution, so its `die "CODE_BIN is set to '…' but that is not runnable"` only exits the subshell. The non-zero status then triggers the caller's `|| die`, and the user sees the precise message immediately followed by "VS Code was not found" plus advice to install the shell command — which is not their problem.
findings.suggestion: Consider having `find_code` `return 1` after printing the CODE_BIN-specific warning (or set a flag the caller checks), so only one diagnosis reaches the user.

findings.title: LINE_BREAK is an obfuscated spelling of /\r?\n/
findings.description: `new RegExp(String.fromCharCode(13) + "?" + String.fromCharCode(10))` builds the same regex the removed literal expressed directly, but a reader now has to decode two char codes to see it. If the intent was to dodge a lint rule or a build-time transform, that reason isn't recorded anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Consider `const LINE_BREAK = /\r?\n/;`, or a short comment naming the constraint that forced the indirect construction.

findings.title: "startup failed" still collapses to the bare "inactive" this change removes
findings.description: `extension.ts:302` calls `dormant("startup failed — see the log")`, which matches none of the branches and falls through to `"inactive"` — the exact status text the comment at line 63 says sends people round a useless disable/reload loop. Startup failure is arguably the state where naming the cause matters most.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding a branch for it before the fallback.
